facts.statement: Leidyosuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodilian from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta, classified as either an alligatoroid or a stem-group crocodilian.
facts.quote: Leidyosuchus (meaning "Leidy's crocodile") is an extinct genus of eusuchian, either an alligatoroid crocodilian or a stem-group crocodilian, from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 1907 by Lawrence Lambe, with L. canadensis designated as the type species.
facts.quote: It was named in 1907 by Lawrence Lambe, and the type species is L. canadensis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Leidyosuchus are known from the middle Campanian age Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from a number of specimens from the middle Campanian age Dinosaur Park Formation.

facts.statement: Leidyosuchus is considered one of the most basal members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.
facts.quote: Leidyosuchus is one of the basal-most members of the superfamily Alligatoroidea.

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Jules D. Walter and colleagues argues that Leidyosuchus may not be a true alligatoroid or even a true crocodilian, but rather a derived non-crocodilian eusuchian that split from the lineage leading to Crocodilia before Deinosuchus.
facts.quote: In a 2025 study, however, Jules D. Walter and colleagues argue that many character states previously thought to be diagnostic for alligatoroids were actually much more widespread. In their analysis several genera traditionally viewed as basal alligatoroids, among them Leidyosuchus, were found to not only fall outside of Alligatoroidea but to not even be true crocodilians, instead representing derived non-crocodilian eusuchians.

facts.statement: The time range for Leidyosuchus is estimated from the Santonian to the Danian, spanning 85.7 to 63.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Danian (85.7 to 63.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 47 recorded fossil occurrences of Leidyosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
In 2026, researchers described the morphology of the endocranial structures of Leidyosuchus canadensis.
facts.quote: Donzé et al. (2026) describe the morphology of endocranial structures of Leidyosuchus canadensis and Stangerochampsa mccabei.

rejected.statement: Leidyosuchus was a medium-sized alligatoroid with a maximum skull length exceeding 40 centimeters (16 inches).
rejected.quote: It was a medium-sized alligatoroid, with a maximum skull length greater than 40 centimeters (16 in).
